justification: Assessment returned INVALID and pinned the defect at line 0001, 'Let 0_G be the identity of the semigroup (G,+)', noting the theorem is stated for a commutative topological semigroup, which need not have an identity, and that the whole padding argument (f = (g_1, 0_G), h = (0_G, g_2), lines 0003-0013 and the cancellation at 0027-0037) collapses without one. That is exactly the ground-truth flaw ('The assumed commutative topological semigroup has an identity element 0_G'). Its witness differs from the ground-truth witness but is independently valid: (R_{>0}, +) with the subspace topology is closed, associative, commutative, and jointly continuous, and has no identity since x + y > x for all x, y > 0; with I={1}, J={2}, g_1=g_2=1 the finite generalized sums converge, so the hypotheses hold while 0_G does not exist. A different-but-valid witness for the same claim counts as matching.
